utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please be seated. Mr. Registrar, have the accused brought in, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do the interpreters hear me? Good morning. Good morning to everybody. Starting out with Mr. Greaves, are you better now, Mr. Greaves; almost completely? I hope it's not your ears that are having a problem this morning. I am very sorry to bring you back into the world of everyday life, which is this trial. Do you feel better now, Mr. Greaves?

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Not perfect, but I'm happy to continue, thank you, and I accept Your Honours' apologies for returning me to the land of reality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Since everybody is in good health now, at least I assume so, we can continue. I suggest that we resume with the cross-examination of Witness G. That is the witness who was being examined by Mr. Greaves when he said that he could not continue. Mr. Registrar, is the witness available?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The registrar is reminding me that it is Witness D. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness D, you are back now. Let me remind you that you are still under protective measures. Try to relax. Be calm, be peaceful. You are being asked questions by the Defence, and I would also remind you that you are still under oath. Mr. Greaves, would you resume, please, at the point where you were forced to leave off yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Mr. Greaves:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness D, I would like to ask you, please, about a description that you gave of the man you described as Goran Jelisic, Adolf. Is this right, that when you spoke to the Office of the Prosecutor in 1995, you described him as someone with an average build, with a very high forehead; do you recall giving that description?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You went on to describe him, his height and his being clean shaven, and you described him as being about 35 years old. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is, 35 years old in 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the person you described as being 35 then would be about 42 now, seven years later?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to ask you now, please, about the murder of Stipo Glavocevic and the description which you give of it. Can you help us with this, please: When describing that incident to the Office of the Prosecutor, you described him as having been brought in and beaten in your presence, but when making a statement to the authorities of Bosnia-Herzegovina, you made no such mention of a beating. Can you explain why you didn't mention that to the authorities in Bosnia-Herzegovina some three years before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: According to you, it was a Serb guard, Serbian guard, who took Stipo Glavocevic out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, with Goran and Kosta Simonovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was a rifle shot which you heard, a loud shot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. Silencer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As if from a rifle as opposed to any other sort of weapon; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. What I heard was a shot fired from a pistol with a silencer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I want to ask you now is this: Again, when making your statement to the authorities of Bosnia-Herzegovina in November 1992, you made no mention whatever of hearing a rifle shot, or a shot, or a silenced shot of any kind. Can you explain the difference between your account to the Office of the Prosecutor and to the Bosnia-Herzegovina authorities, Mr. D?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Greaves, I believe that the witness has made several statements about what he considers to be the difference between the statements that have been produced. Perhaps you should try to move forward in another way than asking what is always a difference. You showed that there was a difference. It's in the transcript. The Judges have taken cognisance of that. I think that he's explained and he's answered you on that point.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Your Honour, there will be one other point which I want to raise which is an important one. It's not just at the moment, but I'll come to it, and you will understand why it is important, I think, in due course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to ask you now, please, Mr. D, about Kosta Simonovic. Would you describe that person to us, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me for interrupting again, but that individual, I believe, was not really very much concerned with in the examination in chief. Perhaps we could move forward. What point do you want to question the witness about? Do you plan to do this for a long time still? Would you explain to the Trial Chamber, what it is that you're trying to do?

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Your Honour, he's named an individual. That's an individual about whom you're going to hear quite often in the course of this case. I want to see if this person is a reliable witness, whether he can recall properly whether he's got the right person or not, so in order to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: -- do that, we have to have a description from him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. All right, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. D. Would you like me to repeat the question to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. D, I want to ask you about Kosta Simonovic, and you said, I think, that you weren't able to describe him.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: Right now, I am not in a position to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many times did you see him whilst you were at Luka?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: I saw him every day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you cannot now recall what he looked like or any other description of him at all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: I could perhaps a little bit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Help us with what you can, please, Mr. D.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: He was between 160 and 170 centimetres tall. He was changing his uniform; sometimes police, sometimes military uniforms. Then he also was carrying a rifle and a baton.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how old was he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: Somewhere between 25 and 30.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to ask you now, please, about your being interrogated at the camp. In all, how many interrogations were conducted with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: Three times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were there, to your knowledge, other detainees interrogated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, there were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the interrogation start on the 8th of May?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did they start then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: On the 9th or 10th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was everybody interrogated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I want to ask you is this, please,

utterances.speaker: MR. D
utterances.text: When you made your statement to the Bosnia-Herzegovina authorities, you told them that a number of interrogations took place on the 8th of May. Does that refresh your memory?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me refresh you further. What you've said was they interrogated all persons and subsequently let them go home. Do you recall that now?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: They didn't let anybody go home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when you told the BiH authorities that people had been released, that was not correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: They did not let anybody go. One they released, but then they brought him back to Luka subsequently.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, let's just clarify this. The truth of the matter is that on the 8th of May, there were people who were released; some may have been brought back at a later date. Is that it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: Only one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, what I want to put to you is this: What you told the Bosnia-Herzegovina authorities was that a number of prisoners were released without interrogation, including people that you knew: Sefko Osmic, Suljo and Suad Osmanovic, and two elderly men whom you did not know. So what you just told Their Honours wasn't correct; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: They were released on the 9th of May.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As to interrogations of other detainees, Mr. D, did you become aware, through speaking to any of them, as to what the purpose of those interrogations was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So there was no discussion at all amongst the prisoners about them having gone for interrogation and come back? They didn't say anything at all about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When people were released, were they given passes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: The one who was released did get a pass, and those who were released on the 9th of May, I'm not sure whether they received passes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many people would you say were released on the 9th of May?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: Four or five.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this correct, that throughout your stay at Luka, there were detainees coming into the camp and detainees going out of the camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: They were taking them somewhere; I don't know where. They were coming and they were being taken away, but I don't know where.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like to turn now, please, to the beating of Naza Bukvic, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to ask you, please, is this right, that the focus of their interest in her was the whereabouts of her brother?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that was absolutely central to what was going on; they were demanding to know where he was. And was that because he was involved in some sort of military activity, or part of the resistance movement, or what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: He was a former policeman in Bosnia-Herzegovina. He was a police officer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was there anything else at all that formed the background to that beating and killing, or was that the only reason at all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: The only reason was the fact that the brother was in the police force.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like to turn now, please, if we may, to Jasce Curmurovic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's right that you told the Office of the Prosecutor about that killing, but you made no mention at all of having been a witness to that, or that incident, to the Bosnia-Herzegovinian authorities; do you accept that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: He was taken out on the 8th of May, in the afternoon, and killed by Goran.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Later in your stay, were you aware of people being released?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you help us, please, about the man -- a man called Pudic? Was he someone you saw at the camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe that man to us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: He was shortish and weighed about 95 kilos. He lived --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't hear the name of the place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were personally interrogated on three separate occasions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The first occasion, was that conducted by four different people who were in a room with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you went for your first interrogation, was there someone else there, another detainee?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, there was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know that detainee?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can I refresh your memory from what you told the BiH authorities: Was it the son of somebody that you knew, Zekerija Tursunovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: I was there, but I was not in the room when they were interrogating the son of Zekerija Tursunovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not suggesting that you were there during his interrogation but that he was there when you were brought in for interrogation. Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The first interrogation that was conducted with you, Mr. D, again, the focus of that interrogation, would this be right, that those people wanted to know about extremist Muslims?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who amongst the Muslim population possessed guns and weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were able to tell them about a number of named individuals; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One of whom, at least, was a former member or a reserve member of the police force?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They also wanted to know if you could identify those who were officials or members of the SDA; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were able to tell them about one particular individual who had been a treasurer in the local community before all this happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this also right, that they also focused upon anybody who might belong to what were described as the Green Berets, a particular military formation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And again, those were essentially the only or the main topics upon which you were interrogated on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who your principal interrogator was on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: The first time, it was Kosta Simonovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On your second interrogation, is this correct, you were asked about a particular individual who had been a former police inspector, and you were told that you could save your life if you informed on his whereabouts?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were again questioned about the identities of what were described as extremist Muslims?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again, I won't mention the name unless I need to refresh your memory. They were interested in another particular family; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: Two families.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Two families. Why were they particularly interested in these two families? Was that explained to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: They were with the SDA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then in respect of your third interrogation, would this be correct, that the focus of the interview was who was in the HOS and where they were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again, further questioning about those who might belong to the formation called the Green Berets. Was your final interrogation on the 14th of May?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was conducted by, I think, a man called Dragan Zivkovic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, an inspector of the former police. That is what he was, with the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was a regular interrogator at the camp; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: He was the last interrogator. They were taken then to another office to be interrogated by him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again, you were taken over the same ground that you had been over with the other interrogators, and I won't repeat what those subjects were. But all those subjects which you had been questioned about before, those were examined again by this individual?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: He interrogated me about the same things as Goran and Kosta previously.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to turn now to the list of people which you were asked about by my learned friend and just see if you can fill in any further details. You told us about a man called Jukic, and you described him as having been killed at home. From whom did you hear that information?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: I heard that from a Serb.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you remember when it was that you heard that information?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: Sometime in late May.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the Serb who was telling you this, did he give you any more information other than he had been killed at home, such as who had killed him or what the circumstances were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then Galib Muranjkovic, he was detained at Luka with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: After me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So he wasn't there with you but was subsequently detained after you had been given release?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you heard from someone else about that matter?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: His brother.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: His brother. How long after your release did you hear that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: After I was exchanged, six months later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Six months later. So sometime in November or December 1992, you heard that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: November.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's all that you know about his fate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Similarly, somebody called Pezerovic who you believed to have been killed at Luka, again was that after -- were you in the camp with him or was that something that must have happened after you had been released?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: He was brought to Luka from the hospital, and they killed him after I had been released.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From whom did you hear that information?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: From a Serb again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Help us with this: Can you say when it was that you heard that information?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: Late May.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Enver Residovic, who you believed had been killed at home, but you don't know any of the circumstances?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. He was killed at home. I know nothing about the circumstances.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again, who told you about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: A Serb again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When were you told about it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: Late May.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then in relation to somebody called Tursunovic, you know that he was killed in his home?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tursunovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: Was it Tursunovic? Suljevic, Hamdija Suljevic?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I've written it down as T-U-R-S-U-N-O-V-I-C, Tursunovic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: Oh, Sefket Tursunovic, killed at home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again, did you know anything more about the circumstances of that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Concerning his son, again killed at home?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: Sefket's son was killed at home, and Zekerija and his son Nijaz were also at home when they were killed. And Sefket is this Zijad's uncle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then Ahmet Hodzic, known as Papa, he was a businessman. You heard from someone else that he had been killed in front of the police station?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From whom did you hear that information?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: A Serb.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Husein Kaknjo? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know what happened to him. Before the retirement, he worked for a company. He was in Brcko during the war, but I don't know what happened to him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he involved in the board of the Islamic Community, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: Something of sorts, yes. He did hold a post.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ahmet Hodzic, was he involved in local politics as president of the local executive in Kolobara?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to turn, please, to Suljevic, Hamdija. I believe that he was killed at home.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again, was he someone who was involved with the board of the Islamic Community?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then Sakib Edhemovic, you heard that he was killed in the town somewhere?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would this be right? I think he was a surgeon. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. He was a well-known surgeon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A prominent man in the town; would that be right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, prominent.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he involved in SDA politics, do you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps I should just clarify that. You don't know whether he was or not, or he wasn't involved in politics?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: He wasn't actively involved.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just going back for a moment, as far as Dr. Edhemovic was concerned, when did you hear that he had been killed and from whom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: I heard that after I was exchanged. He stayed behind me in Brcko, and when I was exchanged, I heard about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then Osman Vatic, I think he was a lawyer.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was killed in Brcko?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again, do you know when it was that he was killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know the date, but I think it was in June.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: June 1992 or 1993?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Finally, is this right? He was a member of the SDA and, I think, also a member of parliament in Brcko.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to ask you about the 14th of May, 1992, again, about just one more matter. Did you ever see a guard at the camp with a ponytail? It may have been somebody called Enver Sok.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How often did you see him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: A couple of times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware of him being involved in beatings or any sort of violence towards anybody?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. D, I want to ask you this, please: As far as you are concerned, the man Goran Jelisic was a central character, the most central character, in your stay at Luka; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... according to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Yes, according to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The person who featured not just every day but many times every day in your stay at Luka?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You knew him as Adolf and as Goran Jelisic when you were there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. That is how he introduced himself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... you heard threatening to kill balijas, making threats against the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then, please, would you be so kind as to help Their Honours with this? When you made a statement to the authorities in Bosnia-Herzegovina, you mentioned him just three times, and then only as "Adolf". If he was so important, why didn't you make more mention than that of him when you were questioned by the authorities in November 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: I may have mentioned him three times. When I was interrogated in 1992, they did not ask for names and all that; they just took some general notes, and he introduced himself as Goran Jelisic on the 8th of May.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As far as that statement was concerned, you never mentioned the name at all of Goran Jelisic; just "Adolf."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, they knew who was meant by that, "Adolf." They knew that when one said "Adolf" that it was Goran Jelisic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me just make it absolutely plain. The three matters in connection with which you mentioned him were these: The killing of your brother, the killing of Stipo, and a beating and interrogation of you. Just those three things. What I'm going to suggest to you, Mr. D, is this: That as far as his role at the camp is concerned, the evidence which you have given to this Tribunal is grossly exaggerated. Do you accept that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOCHILOVSKY
utterances.text: First, with regard to the last question, I think it was a misunderstanding from the accused -- on the witness side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I would like that to be repeated, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOCHILOVSKY
utterances.text: Or I can just ask the

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would prefer that the Defence ask the question again. Thank you, Mr. Tochilovsky. Mr. Greaves, I am asking the witness also to concentrate. Relax, Witness D. All the questions are important, but this one is particularly so, and that is why I'm asking Mr. Greaves to reformulate the question, slowly, giving it in detailed form in respect of his statements before the government of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and then before the Prosecutor, and today under oath. I, myself, was going to ask Witness D: Before the government of Bosnia and Herzegovina, did you take an oath? This is the Presiding Judge speaking to you, asking you that question. Did you take an oath before the government officials of Bosnia-Herzegovina? Mr. Greaves, ask the question very clearly, explain it, and I ask Witness D to concentrate and focus on the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness D, let me put this to you quite clearly. You have given evidence here at the Tribunal about the role which Goran Jelisic, you claim, played at the camp at Luka, and you've described him as being a central character. I suggest to you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, Mr. Greaves. My learned colleague is saying that the answer to my own question was not interpreted and indicated in the transcript. Witness D, you said that you did not take an oath when you made your statement before the government of Bosnia and Herzegovina; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Is --
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. You didn't take an oath. Thank you, Judge Riad. Mr. Greaves, would you start again, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. D, the evidence that you've given here at the Tribunal describes the role that you claim Goran Jelisic played at the camp at Luka, and you've identified that as a central role and him being the central character. What I suggest to you is that you have grossly exaggerated, when giving your evidence at this Tribunal, you have grossly exaggerated the role that Goran Jelisic played.

utterances.speaker: Is --
utterances.text: It is my impression that it was the camp commander, and my authorities slightly added to it when they interrogated me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You aren't answering the question. I'm sorry, you're not answering Mr. Greaves' question.

utterances.speaker: Is --
utterances.text: He was the camp commander.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Greaves is asking you -- and he is entitled to do so -- says that the statements that you made before the Office of the Prosecutor or here are highly exaggerated in respect of the statement that you made to the government of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Do you agree with what Mr. Greaves is saying to you, or do you not agree with what he is saying to you?

utterances.speaker: Is --
utterances.text: They are not exaggerated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is Mr. Greaves' opinion. Do you agree with Mr. Greaves, or do you not agree with Mr. Greaves?

utterances.speaker: Is --
utterances.text: I do not agree with him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And could you explain why you don't agree with him?

utterances.speaker: Is --
utterances.text: Because we're talking about two things. Whether ours exaggerated it, that is, whether our authorities exaggerated it when I made my statement to them, or those of the Tribunal. And I want to say that the people from this Tribunal did not exaggerate it, and what they said is correct, and it was exaggerated by our authorities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Greaves?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You may not have taken an oath when making the statement to the authorities in Bosnia-Herzegovina, but you did sign the statement, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: Is --
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you had made a declaration in the following terms, I suggest, at the end of the statement: "Finally, I declare that here I have stated my personal observations and that everything I have said is true and correct, which I shall confirm with my signature, standing prepared to repeat it in court or before an international organisation which might be interested. I have no complaints against the treatment by the officials." What you were telling the authorities of Bosnia-Herzegovina, I suggest, was that this was your clear recollection of events which you had observed. You were confirming the truth of what you had said in your statement to them.

utterances.speaker: Is --
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And so, three years later when you make your statement and seven years later when you come to give evidence about it, the position has changed, and it's no longer just three matters that you recall, but all these other ones?

utterances.speaker: Is --
utterances.text: It's all right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You gave evidence a moment or two ago about --

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Your Honour, just give me a moment, please. Would Your Honour just give me a moment, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Greaves, have you finished, Mr. Greaves? Thank you very much. Before we take a break, I would like to give the floor to Mr. Tochilovsky again. I'm sorry I interrupted you, but I think the point was important.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOCHILOVSKY
utterances.text: Your Honours, just a few very quick questions to Witness D, because the Defence cross-examination, a substantial part of the cross-examination was about interrogations of the witness, and in response to the Defence, the witness mentioned that he was interrogated three times, and he provided the interrogators with some names and information. Re-examined by Mr. Tochilovsky:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would ask Witness D the following questions. First, Witness D, were you beaten at those interrogations?

utterances.speaker: Is --
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Goran Jelisic participate in those interrogations?

utterances.speaker: Is --
utterances.text: On the second occasion, during the second interrogation, he was there alone with Monika and her mother, Vera, and during the first one was Kosta Simonovic, and on the third was Dragan Zivkovic and someone else, but I didn't know who that was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Goran Jelisic beat you during the interrogation?

utterances.speaker: Is --
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very shortly, can you describe the beating by Goran Jelisic? In short.

utterances.speaker: Is --
utterances.text: He hit me over my head, on the body. He forced me to sign a statement which had not been written down, and then he kept beating me, so I had to do it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOCHILOVSKY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Let me turn to my colleagues now. Judge Riad? Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness D. You may recall that at the beginning of your statements yesterday, you mentioned that Goran Jelisic announced that he will kill as many balijas as possible upon his arrival at Luka, if I have caught you rightly. You did not give any precision. Did he announce, for instance, that he would kill men only, or that he would kill those who were fighting, the fighters, or it was a general declaration concerning all the balijas without specification? Do you recall exactly what this declaration was, the declaration of Goran Jelisic?

utterances.speaker: Is --
utterances.text: He said to kill as many balijas as possible. He did not specify whether there were women, whether there were those who had been fighting. He just said he would kill as many balijas as possible, regardless of whether they were fighters or they had been detained and who were not fighting, but he said that he would kill a lot of balijas.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Without reservation? Do you hear me?

utterances.speaker: Is --
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: All right. But now, do you recall that some people were spared and some people were chosen?

utterances.speaker: Is --
utterances.text: There were a few who were spared. The ones who had been brought by Pudic, they were released, but then those two were later killed at their homes: Zekerija Tursunovic and Zijad Tursunovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: It seems also that there were some differences between the evidence you gave in Bosnia and between your statements here to the Prosecutor's office. What was the purpose of the evidence you gave at Bosnia? What did they want to know from you?

utterances.speaker: Is --
utterances.text: Just some things about the people who were killed, who were tortured.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: They were not mainly interested in Goran Jelisic?

utterances.speaker: Is --
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: They were? Was it the main reason of your evidence there, the way it is here?

utterances.speaker: Is --
utterances.text: It was to account for the victims who were killed by Goran and some others, and this is why I gave the statement. It was on those facts that I testified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: You did not say all the facts then, did you? Did you not have time to say all the facts? Or they did not want it?

utterances.speaker: Is --
utterances.text: They did not ask for all the facts. They just wanted something like bullet points, and they were writing it down; who did what, what did he do with me. And then they put together -- they drafted a statement, and I signed it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: So you were only answering questions there, only answering the questions they asked?

utterances.speaker: Is --
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Judge Riad. Judge Rodrigues? Please proceed, Judge Rodrigues.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone to his honour, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me. As regards the statements given to the authorities of Bosnia-Herzegovina, I also have a few questions. Perhaps I'm going to repeat a few that were already asked by my colleague, Judge Riad. I would like for you to go back and speak about the conditions under which you gave that statement. In general, do you remember what the circumstances were? In general terms, could you give us a kind of general framework within which that statement was made?

utterances.speaker: Is --
utterances.text: This was done hastily. There was shelling going on around, so this was just done sort of like bullet points, and they were then drafting it. It was asked who did they kill, why did they kill; that was very brief. And then when I said that, then they later on added things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] More specifically now, how much time went by after you left the Luka camp?

utterances.speaker: Is --
utterances.text: You mean when I went to the free territory?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The time between the time you left Luka and the time that you made the statements.

utterances.speaker: Is --
utterances.text: Seven months.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me. I did not get the interpretation -- all right. Seven months. Who was the individual to whom you made the statement? Was that person a prosecutor, a policeman, an administrator? Who was he? A judge?

utterances.speaker: Is --
utterances.text: It was the security service.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps he was a policeman then. A civilian or a policeman?

utterances.speaker: Is --
utterances.text: A civilian who worked with a policeman.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A civilian who worked with the police. You have already said something to this effect. This person, did he tell you the following: "You are here in order to explain something." Did he explain to you why you were there?

utterances.speaker: Is --
utterances.text: Just for me to give them some explanations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Therefore, you already answered Judge Riad, but you were only answering the questions that they were asking you? Is that how it was or is that not how it was?

utterances.speaker: Is --
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Another thing. How many people were present to make statements?

utterances.speaker: Is --
utterances.text: Two.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] How many people? I'm thinking about people who were there to give statements. There was a line, and were you alone or were there many people who were waiting to give statements? How was it done?

utterances.speaker: Is --
utterances.text: I don't know. I was alone when I gave the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When you signed the statement, did the person who was there, the civilian, did that person read out loud what you had written? Did he ask you whether you agreed? Did he explain what you said after you said it? How did it proceed?

utterances.speaker: Is --
utterances.text: Nothing was read to me. I just signed it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Therefore, as regards the piece of paper that that civilian wrote, were there already words written on it or was it a blank piece of paper? Was it a type of form, a pre-written form, or was it a blank piece of paper?

utterances.speaker: Is --
utterances.text: A statement had been written out, and I did not read it, they did not read it, and they said, "This is what came out of your questioning. Please sign." And that's what I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With the policeman or with the civilian, were there any attorneys present who could ask you questions? Were there or were there not?

utterances.speaker: Is --
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think I have no further questions. Thank you, Witness D. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Judge Riad. Thank you, Judge Rodrigues. Witness D, we are finished. I have no further questions. All the questions were asked by my colleagues. I thank them for having done so. It's difficult to come to The Hague, and the ordeal is over now. We would like to thank you very much for having taken your time to do so and for having used your mental energy to come to relate these painful memories to us. We wish you Godspeed home and a calmer and more serene life. Once again, thank you. Please do not move, because we have to protect you to the end. It is time to take a 20-minute break, and we will resume at 10.35 for the cross-examination. I see that Mr. Greaves is standing.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We keep making mistakes. It's the cross-examination of Witness E. But I see that Mr. Greaves is asking for the floor again. Yes, Mr. Greaves.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: We would invite exhibition of the statement made to the District Court at Tuzla as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOCHILOVSKY
utterances.text: Your Honours, in this case, we would require both statements, both the OTP statement and the Bosnia-Herzegovina statement, attached as exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That seems fine to me. No other comments. We will take all the statements. The Judges will be very interested in seeing them in order to corroborate what was said during the discussions here. All right, Mr. Registrar, will you give a reference number to the three statements. I think there's the one for the tribunal at Tuzla and the two statements at the Office of the Prosecutor. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You will do that during the break. You should take a break as well, you deserve one, and we will take a good 20-minute break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We will now resume the hearing. Please have the accused brought in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Be seated. I assume that we have the two legal specialists from the Defence team who are both prepared to conduct the cross-examination, but perhaps Mr. Greaves will resume, himself. But it's as you prefer.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, before Mr. Greaves resumes, may I deal with one issue of an exhibit that should be tidied up? I've explained the position to Mr. Greaves and, indeed, to a legal officer. It relates to the pass that the witness produced, Exhibit 24, and for reasons of witness protection and anonymity, the exhibits produced have all been blanked out as to his name. But, of course, that means that you can't be satisfied that it's his pass. So the first thing I've done is had produced the original, which is a document that will be under seal, will be exhibited as 24 bis, and unless my friends wish the witness to look at it specifically in order to identify his name and the fact that it was his pass, then it can probably go in without being further examined by the witness. However, yesterday, when we were looking at the exhibit, there was one part of it that wasn't put on the ELMO which should go on the ELMO and be looked at, and so when the Court has considered 24 bis, which bears the witness's name, I would ask for 24, the one that doesn't bear his name, to go onto the ELMO so that we can see the one passage of the pass that was not looked at yesterday and in respect of which I have two questions to ask. Can we have, please -- it's the very bottom part of the pass. You'll have to put it up a little bit further, please, Mr. Usher. There we are.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Nice:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the bottom of this pass, Witness E, is there some writing that begins "PS"? Witness E, can you see that writing at the bottom of the pass?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I see what is written.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you read it out for us, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E (Resumed)
utterances.text: It says "100 per cent checked," and then it's signed by Adolf.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I haven't received a good interpretation in French. There is a nuance here which I think I am missing. "100 per cent interrogated," in my own language, "Adolf," that would mean "Let him go; I really fully interviewed him and he can go." But my translation is that the person in question is 100 per cent reliable. Of course there is a connection between them, but it's not quite the same thing. But I think that this has to be checked.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I think, Your Honour, if I may respectfully say, so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The word "cist" needs to be translated. The witness -- I don't know that he read that word out, but it may be a word of some importance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the word immediately after "100 per cent," please, Witness E?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E (Resumed)
utterances.text: "Cist." "Clean." "Guarantee for him. Adolf."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And whose writing was this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E (Resumed)
utterances.text: Adolf's. He wrote it for me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you left the camp, as you've told us, did you have to pass through checkpoints?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E (Resumed)
utterances.text: I passed through the Serbian line and then through the Muslim line, and I came out into the free territory with this document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this pass looked at?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, because it was war over at that time, so for me it was either to pass through alive or not, along with my wife and child.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Did you use this pass?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E (Resumed)
utterances.text: My wife had this certificate in her purse, and when I came into the free territory, they were taken away from me, it was taken away from me, because they believed that I was part of the fifth column and that I had been sent by them over here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but before you were with your wife, when you left the camp, when you left Luka, were you able to use this pass to --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E (Resumed)
utterances.text: I came in the evening, and then immediately the next morning, I fled.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you used the pass?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. What did I need it for when I went to flee? I didn't use it until it was taken away from me in the free territory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Those are the only supplementary questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Nice. I still have a translation problem here. Perhaps we could go back to it. The English version says, "100 per cent clean and vouched for," that is, guaranteed. I'm not sure that there's an absolute match between the Serbo-Croat, French, and English versions. I think this is relatively important, because one can interpret the accused's role in the camp in various ways, depending upon whether he is giving a guarantee or whether he simply conducted a 100 per cent interview. So I would like the Serbo-Croat version to be used as the basis for a retranslation which will be definitive.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the Serbo-Croat version, we see the word "guarantee." Could the French booth, using what they see on the screen, translate or interpret for me into French or English exactly how that should be translated from the language of the accused at the time of the facts? Would that be possible?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Somebody needs to read it out loud, word for word.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Was I heard? Does the French booth hear me? I see that you're concentrating on the sentence.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: It states, "P.S.: 100 per cent clean. I guarantee for him. Adolf."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. I think there are no further comments. I will note that. So that for me, as far as I'm concerned, it means "guarantee." I'm assuming that's what it means and then that it's 100 per cent clear. I think that the English version perhaps is a better match with the original than the French. Well, we're not going to speak any further about that. We won't dwell on that any longer. It's clear for me. Mr. Nice, did you want to add something?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Only this, Your Honour, that if -- the Court might want to know from the witness whether he can help at all with his understanding of the word "clean," he being there at the time. Because "clean" and "being guaranteed for" are not necessarily synonymous.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wanted to know how it should be translated in my own system. In my own system, in fact, we would only ask the witness, but we can't do that. All right, I'm going to ask the witness. You saw other mercy passes, and I know these were very difficult circumstances for you. How should that sentence be interpreted? Would Adolf put the same thing on all the mercy passes? But what did it mean for you, specifically? Could you explain to us exactly what it meant for you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E (Resumed)
utterances.text: I only know that he issued it to me and that he wrote "100 per cent questioned," or "interrogated," and then he gave it to me to take it home so I can go and feed my wife and child, and I only know that he issued it to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And the line beneath that?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: This is the Judge speaking to the French booth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. I think that we can now move to the cross-examination. Do you agree, Mr. Nice? Thank you very much. Thank you, Witness E. Mr. Greaves, you can now conduct your cross-examination. About how long are you going to need?

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Perhaps an hour or an hour and a half.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. All right, you're not taking many risks. When you say an hour, an hour and a half, it's like saying an hour to two hours, but all right; I did say approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Your Honour, can I just deal with the question of the pass whilst we've just been dealing with it? As I understand it, yesterday afternoon, an exhibit was made of one where the name is expunged, and at the present time, the Tribunal has within its possession two translations: One in English, one in French. Your Honour has challenged the translation, and we've now clarified what the translation of the final line is. The exhibit should be withdrawn and replaced by one which bears that corrected translation, in my submission, and I wonder whether my learned friend could possibly arrange for it to be retyped and resubmitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: While I'm on my feet, if at all possible, this witness would be able to and I'm sure would like to return home tomorrow morning, if that's possible. He has been here a whole week.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: I had that very much in mind, that it would be desirable to finish this witness today. It's not desirable to leave witnesses over the weekend, and I will do my, of course, best to ensure that situation is brought about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Let me remind you that theoretically we work until 1.30, so let's try to do everything that we can so that Witness E can return home tonight. Mr. Greaves, please proceed. Cross-examined by Mr. Greaves:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. E, I would like to ask you first of all, please, as you were asked yesterday about the circumstances of your arrest. But before I do that, can I just ask you to do this, please: If I ask you a question which you do not understand or confuses you, please don't hesitate. Tell me straight away, and I will rephrase it so that it's an easier question for you to deal with. All right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The request is, don't be shy; if you don't understand, sing out immediately. As far as you, personally, are concerned, can I just ask you a little bit about you? Before the war which broke out in May 1992 in the Brcko district, were you in any way involved in political life? Were you a member of a political party or anything like that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. Never in my life. I was never a member of any party. I'm just a miserable wretch.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, not belonging to a political party doesn't make you a miserable wretch, Mr. E.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And so --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Not even after the war did you ever join any political party?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E (Resumed)
utterances.text: Never. Never.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you serve in the army of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina during the war, or since?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E (Resumed)
utterances.text: In the army, in the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that during the war, or do you continue to be employed as a soldier in the BiH army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, only for the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Concerning your arrest, I don't want to know where exactly you lived at that stage, Mr. E, but just if you can describe this: You didn't live in the main part of the town of Brcko but in a hamlet on the outskirts; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E (Resumed)
utterances.text: The suburb of the town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were arrested during the middle of the day on the 14th of May; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E (Resumed)
utterances.text: At 12.00, in the apartment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think the people who arrested you you identified as Arkanovic because of their uniform.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was particular about their uniform that told you these were Arkanovic or Arkanovci?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E (Resumed)
utterances.text: They had black T-shirts, black jeans, and on the pocket behind, a tiger, a yellow emblem of a tiger.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it just you that they took away or did they take away anybody else from your immediate surroundings?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E (Resumed)
utterances.text: They took me, my neighbour, both him and her, the three of us, and they left my wife and child behind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they examine your identification cards?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E (Resumed)
utterances.text: They only asked the identity card of my wife's. When they saw that I was a Muslim, they told my wife to pack things for me and get me ready. So my wife got ready, and I took the identity card, the discharge document of the hospital, and I brought it there, together with my neighbours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this correct, effectively, that it was male people being taken away but not women?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. The wife went with us to the camp, to Luka, and when we reached Luka, me and my male neighbour were taken there, and my female neighbour, that is, his wife, she left with those people who had brought us there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now I want to ask you, you arrived at Luka at about 1.00; would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E (Resumed)
utterances.text: It is. We arrived in Luka around 1.00. Yes, I think it was about 1.00.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you got there, I firstly ask if you can help me with this: What type of personnel were in charge at the camp? Were they soldiers, police, people from a militia or a special unit? What were they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E (Resumed)
utterances.text: When I entered Luka and when I was taken out, they were men in olive-grey uniforms like the wintertime uniform. Some of them wore multi-coloured uniforms. One small policeman was in a blue uniform with short sleeves, and they were all standing there. The two of us were made to lean against the door of that warehouse, and we were standing, and the one in the multi-coloured uniform came to me and told me to go into the office. When I went into the office, there was a man there sitting, dark with moustache, and he asked to see my documents. He asked me where I came from, and I told him. "Do you have anything else with you?" I said, "No." "Empty your pockets." I emptied my pocket. "You're free to go." I left, and the one in the multi-coloured uniform with long hair again made me lean against the door of that warehouse, and I stood there. Meanwhile, a man appeared with a black briefcase. He went in, and a female. He was wearing a blue uniform, short sleeves, that is, a shirt with short sleeves. The female had a white dress, black tights, and the dress was white with black dots.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we just clarify something you've just said? You've described a man appearing. It's come up on the transcript as "a black briefcase". Did you, in fact, say a man appeared in a car or with a car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, yes, it was a car, a black car. He arrived in a black car from the petrol station and he entered the gate, and he left the car there and continued on foot with that girl.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: I wasn't present yesterday afternoon, but I think this was given an exhibit number. Perhaps I could just ask the usher to show that to you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is Prosecution Exhibit 23.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. E, can I just establish with you, were you made to stand against the door of the warehouse that we can see in the picture there? Just glance over. I think you can probably see it on the video screen. Can you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are those the offices into which you were taken in due course?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E (Resumed)
utterances.text: I was standing here to the left [indicating] and my neighbour to the right, and the one in front here, this door here [indicating], that is the office and that is where people went into the toilet as I was standing there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again, sorry to go into it, but I just want to get it absolutely clear. The door of the hangar we can see is open?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it closed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E (Resumed)
utterances.text: About that much [indicating] just for one to get out. Not more than that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was sufficiently open that one or two people could pass through the door, so about seven-eighths closed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, only one, only one man, only one. It would allow only one man to pass.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long were you kept waiting at that door for?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E (Resumed)
utterances.text: I waited until the one in the multi-coloured uniform approached that policeman and that female and said, "We've got a woman. There she is, sitting on a chair, a balija woman, SDA," and he started off -- now, if we imagine, you know when the wind blows and it's so strong that it takes you away, that is how he started towards that woman, and grabbed her by the scruff of the neck with his left hand, lifted her off and pulled her a bit further away, five or six metres, and pulling and pulling her, and then got out his pistol, and right into the back of her head.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. E, I don't want to stop you from telling us what happened, but it's going to help both you, to get away quicker, and Their Honours, to understand what happened, if you listen to the question and just answer the question. I know you want to tell us as much as you can, but if you can do that, please, we're going to get away quicker. All right? I know that you're anxious, and I'm keen to make you as comfortable as possible. Just answer the question and we'll get on.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E (Resumed)
utterances.text: I answered the question. I said he killed that woman. What else do you want me to say?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The question is this: How long were you kept waiting at the door before you were interrogated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E (Resumed)
utterances.text: What did they interrogate me? They didn't interrogate me at all. I was standing when he killed the woman, and the one with the long hair shouted, "Get into that warehouse." I entered the warehouse, and when I looked, there were lots of people there. In the one corner, there were socks, white socks, some dresses, and there were people sitting there. As you see this door, there's an identical door on the other end, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness E, this is the Presiding Judge speaking to you. I know that we are doing this as absolutely carefully as we can in respect of all the series of things that happened to you, but the Judges must also respect in these proceedings an absolute balance between what the Prosecution wants to prove and what the Defence wants to prove. I'm making this intervention in order to ask you first to answer the questions that are asked. There was a specific question, "How much time did you remain waiting in that place?" You can answer very briefly. I think we're going to get to the point which troubled you the most, and of course we could understand this, as the death of this woman right in front your eyes, but we'll get to it. But for the time being, please try to answer the questions that are being asked very specifically, that is, the questions Mr. Greaves is asking you, and I thank you very much for doing so. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The question, and I'll remind you of it, was how long were you kept waiting at the door before being taken into the office, and whether it was an interrogation or just a series of questions, how long were you there for?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know about time. I don't know about time. I was there -- well, it could have been 15 minutes or so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for having made the effort to give a specific answer. Please proceed, Mr. Greaves.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour, for your assistance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. E, you were taken into the offices. You say it wasn't an interrogation, but you were asked some questions and you handed some documents over; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E (Resumed)
utterances.text: I gave documents to that man and came back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long in all were you inside the offices?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, just as long as it took me to get my documents out of my pocket, give it to them, and when he told me to empty my pockets and to leave the office. So it could have taken how much? Two minutes, not more than that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The person inside the building, was he alone or were there other people in the room with him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, he was alone. That man was alone, and he had a moustache, and he was alone there. But when I entered, there was a huge pile of identity cards. Whatever anyone had was there on his desk.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The man that you saw in that office, was he examining the identity cards, or what was he doing with them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E (Resumed)
utterances.text: Nothing. He was just taking them and piling them up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Help me with this, please, Mr. E: Can you describe for us the man who was in the room with the identification cards? What was his age?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E (Resumed)
utterances.text: He could have been 40-ish, a dark moustache, parted hair, black parted hair.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How was he dressed? Was he in uniform or was he in civilian clothes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. Civilian uniform, a shirt -- well, you know how men dress.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of course. In the course of the conversation that you had with him, did he identify either himself or what he was doing at the camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E (Resumed)
utterances.text: Nothing, nothing, nothing, no. That man said nothing to me. He only asked that, and I gave it to him, and nothing else. He didn't give me his name or anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Help me with this, please: You then became aware of the arrival of a van with this woman inside it. How long had you been waiting? Having been sent outside again, how long before that van arrived?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E (Resumed)
utterances.text: No one in that room -- the black car and the woman, as soon as they arrived, the van turned and left with that woman. I don't know where they went, but only that woman left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The people who had brought her in, were you able to identify whether they were from the military or from a special unit or a militia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, I'm telling him, those men had dark black T-shirts, black trousers, and the emblem of a yellow tiger, and they spoke as Serbians do, people from Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The woman was placed next-door to the offices?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E (Resumed)
utterances.text: That woman who was with me was taken away. But another woman was brought, a blonde woman, 38 to 40 years old, blonde. She was wearing a red vest and a red chequered skirt.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if we may turn to the people who arrived in the black car, did you know the woman who arrived in the black car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. E, I just want to refresh your memory, if you will. It's right, in fact, that you told the Office of the Prosecutor that you recognised the woman arriving in the black car, didn't you? You knew her as Monika?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E (Resumed)
utterances.text: I only know her mother. Her mother worked for the "7th of April". Her mother was Vera, and she was a cleaning woman and chore woman. I know her.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told the Office of the Prosecutor that you knew Monika's brother as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E (Resumed)
utterances.text: Her brother was a house painter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know his name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see the brother at Luka whilst you were there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The person that you say signed your pass with the name "Adolf", would you just describe him to us, please? How old was he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E (Resumed)
utterances.text: Sure, I can. Why not? He could have been 26 to 28 years of age. Yes, that's so, and he weighed about 65 to 70 kilos. Tall, about 180, 190. That's how tall he was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can I remind you again of this, that what you told the Office of the Prosecutor was that he was around 190 centimetres tall, with a thin build?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E (Resumed)
utterances.text: I'm telling you, a rather thin, lanky, tall, skinny man.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you first saw him, was he armed or unarmed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E (Resumed)
utterances.text: He had a rifle about that size [indicating]. I don't know what that weapon was called, but he had that rifle, and that female who came with him had a pistol.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you about not knowing the name of the rifle. Isn't it the case that you told the Office of the Prosecutor that you did, in fact, recognise the weapon; a short-barrelled rifle with small-calibre ammunition called a Zagi?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E (Resumed)
utterances.text: When I arrived in the free territory, I saw that kind of weapon and I asked, "What is this rifle?" They told me, "Zagi," and he had one like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then I think another person came onto the scene, somebody who had a ponytail. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, long hair, ponytail with a rubber band, and he had it tied nicely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know that person at all or was he a complete stranger to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, no, no, no, I didn't know him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever hear him being referred to by any name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E (Resumed)
utterances.text: Not until Adolf came. And when he told him, "Adolf, we've got a woman," then I heard Adolf address him "Sok", and that is how I learned that his name was Sok.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The first thing that was said about the woman was to make a reference to her being an SDA member; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
